newsitem.title: USA: U.S. budget deal to spur long-term growth--Yellen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. budget deal to spur long-term growth--Yellen.

text.p: The newly reached U.S. budget deal should stimulate economic growth in the long run, although results cannot be expected immediately, White House chief economist Janet Yellen told reporters Tuesday.
"In the next five years one shouldn't expect to see anything extraordinary, but I regard this as a very pro-growth budget," the chairwoman of the Council of Economic Advisers said.
Yellen said economic expansion depends on growth in productivity and in the labor supply. The budget should help boost productivity, she said.

"I see this budget agreement as, over the long term, certainly being helpful to productivity by making investments in education and in children that are important to long-term economic growth," Yellen said.
The benefits from such investment can only be felt after a long period of development, she said.
"Those things of course do take a long time -- as long as it takes a child to grow up -- to see a return on investments," Yellen said.
